label: <DEL> step, plus 1/r/y/x/c/e inputs shortly after g/x/e/o (weak)
explanation: Most concentrated at the <DEL> step (4.9x lift, 45% of activation mass), but fires there on only ~25% of sequences. The rest is spread over original and copy steps, driven by the input token (1, r, y, x, c, e are most active; 0, j, m, a rarely) and raised when g, x, e or o appeared one or two steps earlier. Never fires at t=0. Largest activations come at <DEL> or the first copy step after runs of g/x/e/o in the original. What sets the magnitude at <DEL> seems to be a graded function of earlier tokens that no simple predicate captures (prev_tok in g/x/e/o raises <DEL> precision to only 0.42). The best predicate reaches dev F1 0.33 / mass recall 0.64 with precision 0.24, so this is a partial, diffuse description.
